Standard titration (once weekly, subcutaneous)
Weeks 1 to 4: 2 mg once weekly. Weeks 5 to 8: 4 mg. Weeks 9 to 12: 6 mg. Weeks 13 to 16: 9 mg. Week 17 onward: 12 mg as the target maintenance dose. Hold each dose for the full 4 weeks before going up.

dosing_html: Start at 2 mg. In the trials, people who jumped straight to higher doses had far more nausea (around 60%) than those who started low (around 17%), so the slow ramp is the whole point, not a formality.

The newer Phase 3 schedule (shown above) ramps 2, 4, 6, 9, 12 mg, each held 4 weeks, for the smoothest climb. The older Phase 2 trial jumped 2, 4, 8, 12 and skipped the 6 and 9 mg steps, which works but trades tolerability for speed.
Working range across users is roughly 4 mg to 12 mg weekly. 12 mg was the highest dose studied and gave the most weight loss.
Pick one day a week and keep it consistent, since the half-life is about 6 days.

Weeks 1 to 4: 2.5 mg. Weeks 5 to 8: 5 mg. Then step up by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks as needed: 7.5, 10, 12.5, up to 15 mg max. Recommended maintenance doses are 5, 10, or 15 mg. The 2.5 mg step is a starter dose, not a maintenance dose.

protocols.protocol_html:
Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
1 mg to 2 mg per day, once daily or split morning and evening. At a 3 mL fill on the 50 mg vial (about 16.7 mg/mL), 1 mg is a 0.06 mL draw (6 units) and 2 mg is 0.12 mL (12 units). The 100 mg vial at 3 mL is twice as concentrated, so halve those draws. A 5 days on, 2 off pattern is common.
Be patient and inject slowly
GHK-Cu works through gene expression, so visible skin and hair changes take weeks. Commit to a 30 day cycle (then 14 days off), ideally 8 to 12 weeks total, before judging it. It is acidic and can sting, so dilute more and push slowly.

protocols.protocol_html:
How a blend is dosed
You dose GLOW by the amount of GHK-Cu you want, and the BPC-157 and TB-500 come along in the 5:1:1 ratio. The common range is 1 mg to 2.5 mg of GHK-Cu per day, with around 2.5 mg typical during loading. At a 3 mL fill the GHK-Cu portion comes to about 16.7 mg/mL, so 1 mg of GHK-Cu is a 0.06 mL draw (6 units) and 2.5 mg is 0.15 mL (15 units). At 2.5 mg of GHK-Cu you also get about 0.5 mg each of BPC-157 and TB-500. These figures are for the usual 3 mL fill; if you received a 5 mL vial, switch the bac water pill above and the dose helper recalculates every draw for you.
Schedule
One subcutaneous injection daily, or 5 days on, 2 days off, rotating sites. Run an 8 to 12 week block, then 4 to 8 weeks off. Many load daily then drop to 3 times weekly for maintenance. Inject slowly to limit the GHK-Cu sting.

How a blend is dosed
You dose REGEN by the total amount of blend you want, and the BPC-157 and TB-500 come along evenly in the 1:1 ratio. The common range is 0.5 mg to 2 mg of total blend per day, with 1 mg per day a solid middle. On the 10 mg vial at a 2 mL fill (5 mg/mL total), 1 mg of blend is a 0.2 mL draw (20 units), which delivers 0.5 mg each of BPC-157 and TB-500. On the 20 mg vial at 2 mL (10 mg/mL total), the same 1 mg dose is a 0.1 mL draw (10 units).
Schedule and placement
One subcutaneous injection daily, rotating sites. BPC-157 works best near the injury, while TB-500 acts systemically, so for a specific injury you can inject close to the area and still get the whole-body benefit. A 5 days on, 2 days off pattern is common.
Duration
Run a 6 to 12 week block, then take a break. Acute injuries often start responding in 2 to 3 weeks; chronic issues and post-surgical recovery usually take 4 to 8 weeks to show clear progress.

protocols.protocol_html:
Why these two together
CJC-1295 (No DAC) tells the pituitary to make growth hormone, while Ipamorelin tells it to release it, two different signals on the same gland. The No DAC version is used here because its short half-life lines up with Ipamorelin, which keeps the natural pulsing pattern intact. They are combined in one syringe and one shot.
Standard protocol (subcutaneous)
0.1 mg of each peptide before bed is the standard starting dose, moving to 0.2 mg of each for most people. On the 10 mg vial (5 mg of each) at a 2 mL fill, 0.1 mg of each is a 0.04 mL draw (4 units) and 0.2 mg of each is 0.08 mL (8 units). Dose once daily, 5 days on, 2 days off.
Timing matters
Inject before bed, at least 2 hours after your last meal. Food (especially carbs and fat) blunts the GH pulse, and the body releases its own GH overnight, so a fasted bedtime shot lines up with natural timing. A fasted morning or post-workout dose is the other common slot.
Titration and ceiling
Start at 0.1 mg of each and increase by about 0.05 mg every 1 to 2 weeks if you want, up to a common ceiling of 0.3 mg of each per day (0.12 mL / 12 units at the 2 mL fill). 0.1 mg is already a saturating dose for many, so more is not always better.

protocols.protocol_html:
Standard protocol (subcutaneous or intramuscular)
200 mg to 600 mg per injection, 2 to 3 times weekly is the common range for antioxidant and detox support. Skin-brightening protocols run at the higher end. At a 5 mL fill on the 1500 mg vial (300 mg/mL), 200 mg is a 0.67 mL draw (67 units) and 300 mg is a full 1 mL (100 units) on an insulin syringe. A 600 mg dose is 2 mL, which is more than one insulin syringe holds, so split it into two injections or use a 3 mL syringe. Injecting more than about 1.5 mL into a single subcutaneous site tends to leak, so splitting a large dose across two sites is good practice anyway.
Timing and pairing
Morning on an empty stomach is a common choice. Do not mix it in the same syringe as vitamin C, they can react and cloud the solution, so inject them separately if stacking. Some pair it with oral NAC to support the body's own glutathione production.
Duration
Run a loading phase 2 to 3 times weekly for 4 to 8 weeks, then drop to once weekly for maintenance. Since glutathione is made naturally by the body, continuous use is possible, but many run 12 weeks on and 4 weeks off.

protocols.protocol_html:
Wellness and anti-aging (subcutaneous)
1 IU to 3 IU per day, once daily, for recovery, sleep, skin and general anti-aging. At a 1.5 mL fill on a 15 IU vial (10 IU/mL), 1 IU is a 0.1 mL draw (10 units), 2 IU is 0.2 mL (20 units), 3 IU is 0.3 mL (30 units). Start at 1 IU for the first couple of weeks, then work up.
Muscle building and fat loss
2 IU to 4 IU per day is the common performance range, with 4 IU to 6 IU per day used by more serious bodybuilders for mass and fat loss. 4 IU is a 0.4 mL draw (40 units), 5 IU is 0.5 mL (50 units), 6 IU is 0.6 mL (60 units). Higher doses bring more water retention, wrist or hand tingling, and a real risk of insulin resistance, so climb gradually and do not jump straight to the top.
Advanced and competition prep
6 IU is the usual ceiling for most. Around 8 IU per day pushes muscle growth further but side effects climb sharply, so it is reserved for experienced users in short competition runs, often alongside testosterone and sometimes insulin. 8 IU is a 0.8 mL draw (80 units). This is not a starting point.
Dosing schedule and timing
At 1 IU to 3 IU, one daily injection is fine. At 4 IU and up, split it into two injections per day (for example 2 IU morning and 2 IU afternoon at a 4 IU total), 5 to 6 days per week. Do not inject the second dose right before bed: your body releases its own growth hormone overnight, which acts as a natural third pulse, and dosing on top of it blunts that.
Cycle length
HGH works slowly through IGF-1, not as a pre-workout, so noticeable changes take weeks. Bodybuilding runs are commonly 8 to 12 weeks short or 16 to 24 weeks long, with 16 weeks a typical average. Wellness users often run it longer at the low end.

protocols.protocol_html:
TRT protocol (maintenance)
100 mg to 150 mg per week, most commonly split into two equal shots every 3.5 days (e.g. 50 to 75 mg Monday and Thursday). At 250 mg/mL, a 75 mg dose is a 0.3 mL draw on a 3 mL syringe. Subcutaneous or intramuscular.
First cycle (performance, test only)
The classic beginner cycle is 500 mg per week for 12 weeks, test only, nothing else stacked. Split it into two 250 mg shots per week (for example Monday and Thursday). At 250 mg/mL, 250 mg is a 1 mL draw per shot on a 3 mL syringe. Run 12 weeks rather than less: with this ester it takes 4 to 5 weeks just to reach stable blood levels, so shorter cycles waste most of the climb.
Estrogen control on cycle
500 mg/week aromatises, so keep an aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole or aromasin) on hand for estrogen symptoms (puffiness, sore or swollen nipples). Use it only if symptoms show up, not automatically. Pull bloodwork mid-cycle to see where estradiol and hematocrit sit.
Post cycle therapy (PCT)
500 mg/week shuts down your own testosterone, so PCT is not optional. Start 14 days after your last shot (the ester has to clear first). Common protocol: Nolvadex 40 mg/day for 2 weeks, then 20 mg/day for 2 weeks. Clomid is the alternative at 50 mg/day for 2 weeks then 25 mg/day for 2 weeks.
Bloodwork either way
Check total and free testosterone, estradiol and hematocrit at 6 to 8 weeks. On TRT the target trough is roughly 500 to 900 ng/dL. On a 500 mg cycle your levels will sit well above range by design; the point of the bloodwork is watching estradiol and hematocrit, not chasing a trough number.
TRT is meant to be run indefinitely
Unlike a cycle, TRT is not something you come off. At a replacement dose it is an ongoing, long-term protocol: most people stay on it for life once dialled in, pulling bloodwork a couple of times a year to keep their numbers in range.
